subject: Quantica Labs — operational commitments & monthly credit proposal
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@quantica.com>
Cc: procurement@quantica.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantica: operational commitments & monthly credit proposal

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is an initial SLA matrix for the hosted inference endpoints we discussed (SLA_Matrix_QTK_v1.pdf). Highlights of the initial proposal: 

- Interactive/low-latency endpoints (production API): 99.95% monthly uptime SLO.
- Bulk/batched endpoints (scheduled inference jobs): 99.9% monthly uptime SLO (different usage profile and maintenance tolerance).
- Monthly service-credit tiers (applied to affected invoice):
  • < 99.95% and >= 99.5%: 10% credit for the month
  • < 99.5% and >= 99.0%: 25% credit for the month
  • < 99.0%: 40% credit for the month
- Monthly credit cap: typically 15% of monthly invoice (we can discuss higher cap for an introductory pilot).
- Standard maintenance carveouts (pre-scheduled maintenance windows, force majeure, agreed regional network outages).

Two quick asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm which endpoints Quantica will treat as interactive vs. batch (we need the list to tie measurement to routes)?
2) Procurement timeline — are you targeting an August signature or would September be safer?

I looped procurement in to keep your team in the loop. If you want to push for a different uptime target or a different credit cap we can iterate — this is intentionally conservative for hosted & fully-managed usage.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Matrix_QTK_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@quantica.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quantica.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quantica: operational commitments & monthly credit proposal

Rachel — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. A few reactions from Quantica: 

- Our legal & SRE teams are going to push for a stronger interactive SLO — ideally 99.99% for the primary production endpoints that serve customer-facing queries.
- We understand batch behaves differently, but we'd like the monthly credit cap increased — 25% is more acceptable for our procurement team during the first 6 months of the relationship.
- Please add explicit regional measurement language: we need uptime measured from AWS us-east-1 and us-west-2 (our traffic originates there).
- Also, can you provide the SOC2 + penetration test summary as part of the package? Our security folks asked for evidence.

Procurement note: we need final terms before the end of August to hit our internal start date in September.

Best,
Oliver Grant
Head of Infrastructure
Quantica Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quantica: operational commitments & monthly credit proposal — negotiation notes

(routing internal)

Quick notes on negotiation posture for Quantica (QTK-348):

- Do not concede 99.99% for interactive endpoints. 99.99% is effectively five nines work — we'd need dedicated capacity and SLA uplift pricing. Counter: offer 99.95% standard + an optional 99.99% add-on (reserved capacity / higher-tier plan) with explicit pricing.
- On credit cap: agree to a temporary elevated cap (25%) for the first quarter of the contract as a goodwill for the pilot, then step down to 15% ongoing. That buys time for stability tuning while limiting long-term exposure.
- Measurement: accept customer's ask for region-specific measurement but require the clause 'measurement will be per-request routing as defined in Appendix A (customer-provided endpoint list)'.
- Maintenance carveouts: keep pre-scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice and a maximum monthly duration threshold; emergency maintenance permitted with post-incident report.
- Security artifacts: provide SOC 2 Type II summary and latest pentest executive summary; redact sensitive vendor details.

Action items for Rachel:
- Update SLA_Matrix to include the pilot cap language & measurement appendix (I attached a short redline).
- Confirm the commercial uplift pricing for optional 99.99% (estimate: +35% to committed monthly price or as a reserved pool).

Attachment: quantica_sla_redlines.txt (plain text, 3KB)

Ben
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@quantica.com>, procurement@quantica.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Quantica: operational commitments & monthly credit proposal — revised offer

Oliver / Quantica procurement —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on procurement timing and measurement. We've reviewed internally and can offer the following compromise to get you to production without committing Redwood to dedicated provisioning immediately: 

Summary of agreed / proposed terms (attached: SLA_Matrix_QTK_v2.pdf):
- Interactive production endpoints: 99.95% monthly uptime SLO (base plan). Optional upgrade: 99.99% as a paid reserved-capacity add-on (we will provide pricing and capacity delta in a separate addendum).
- Bulk / batched endpoints: 99.9% monthly uptime SLO (explicitly called out in Appendix A).
- Monthly credits (applied to the affected invoice):
  • < 99.95% and >= 99.5%: 10% credit
  • < 99.5% and >= 99.0%: 25% credit
  • < 99.0%: 40% credit
- Monthly credit cap: 20% of invoice for the first 90 days from contract effective date (pilot phase), then 15% thereafter.
- Measurement: uptime measured from the customer's declared primary regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) with request-level routing list maintained in Appendix A. Disputes resolved via mutually agreed monitoring endpoint and 7-day reconciliation window.
- Maintenance carveouts: pre-scheduled maintenance (72-hour notice) and emergency maintenance (post-incident report).
- Security artifacts: attaching SOC 2 Type II executive summary and pentest summary for your security review (redacted where appropriate).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the list of interactive endpoints we should treat as production (simple list of hostnames/paths will do).
2) If agreed, we'll push the SLA appendix and the commercial addendum into DocuSign — link included: https://app.docusign.com/XYZ-Quantica-SLA-QTK-348.
3) If Quantica wants the 99.99% option now, we can provide a pricing addendum (separate negotiation).

If this looks ok I can get legal to turn the redline into contract language today and send for signature to meet your September start.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Matrix_QTK_v2.pdf (PDF, 56KB); SOC2_TypeII_Summary_redacted.pdf (PDF, 220KB); pentest_execsum_redacted.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
